comparability.reason: Pilot-scale continuous foam fractionation treating landfill leachate with documented matrix (landfill leachate), operation mode (continuous enriching/stripping), foam fractions, and PFAS mass-balance metrics provides quantitative information that can be compared to other pilot/full-scale foam fractionation systems treating similar matrices, provided differences in short-chain vs long-chain PFAS composition and wet vs dry foam collection are considered.

endpoints.interpretation: Foam fractionation used as a first-step concentration/removal technology for PFAS in landfill leachate; continuous mode achieved treatment efficiencies comparable to batch mode, with negligible differences between enriching vs stripping modes. Removal of short-chain PFAS was limited; removal of long-chain PFAS higher (qualitative in supplied text).

Mass balance closure for individual PFAS and ΣPFAS between feed, foam, and effluent was assessed; closures for individual continuous-experiment runs ranged from about two-thirds to complete or slightly >100%, and compounds with lower removal (short-chain PFAS) showed better individual mass balance closure.

limitations.statement: Continuous pilot-scale foam fractionation showed limited removal of short-chain PFAS and variable mass balance closure; authors suggest that bubble size control, alternative bubble-generation methods, additives, enhanced foam collection, series operation, and better accounting for PFAS in exhaust air could improve performance and mass balance closure.

Mass balance closure varied considerably between experimental runs and did not correlate with ΣPFAS removal; compounds with lower removal (short-chain PFAS) showed better individual mass balance closure.

Foam collected in continuous mode was relatively wet because % foam was controlled via effluent flow with the foam outlet just above the water–air surface, making the operation a mix of bubble fractionation and foam fractionation.
